findings.claim: The v1.3.3 no-send public bundle has no public release, DOI, or deposit asserted.
findings.failure_mode: The RO-Crate-referenced manifest is still a v1.3.2 public-release manifest: release_id oc_core_1_3_2, version 1.3.2, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19851694, concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17899134, git_tag v1.3.2, and many releases/oc_core_1_3_2 source_path entries. This directly contradicts the v1.3.3 no-send metadata and leaks stale DOI/public payload metadata through the public surface.
findings.required_repair: Regenerate manifest.json from the current v1.3.3 no-send payload: set release_id oc_core_1_3_3 and version 1.3.3, remove or null all DOI/public record fields until owner approval, remove v1.3.2 source/payload entries, and bind it to refreshed v1.3.3 checksums.

findings.claim: The integrity surface verifies the current v1.3.3 no-send payload.
findings.failure_mode: checksums.txt is stale against the current package: it lists .zenodo.json even though that file is absent, and it still includes many oc_core_1_3_2 paths. Because ro-crate-metadata.jsonld includes checksums.txt as a public hasPart, the release integrity surface preserves stale public metadata instead of verifying v1.3.3.
findings.required_repair: Regenerate checksums.txt only from existing v1.3.3 no-send release-critical artifacts after the manifest repair; remove .zenodo.json unless a current v1.3.3 no-send Zenodo draft exists.

findings.claim: Release-critical Zenodo metadata is available for audit and is no-send/owner-gated.
findings.failure_mode: .zenodo.json is absent, while manifest.json and checksums.txt still list it with a stale hash. The Zenodo public-action surface therefore cannot be audited, and stale metadata references can either break verification or resurrect old deposit metadata.
findings.required_repair: Restore a v1.3.3 .zenodo.json draft containing only owner-gated no-send metadata, no DOI/concept DOI/record identifiers, and version 1.3.3, then update manifest.json and checksums.txt to its current hash.

findings.claim: The RO-Crate describes an actual v1.3.3 no-send review bundle.
findings.failure_mode: The RO-Crate hasPart list includes primary_pdfs/, repro/, evidence/, and metadata/ paths that are absent at the crate root, and it includes manifest.json/checksums.txt that are stale v1.3.2 surfaces. The crate therefore advertises a bundle that is not present and is not public-surface-parity clean.
findings.required_repair: Update ro-crate-metadata.jsonld hasPart to the actual current v1.3.3 artifacts, create any intentionally listed package directories, and replace stale manifest/checksum references with regenerated v1.3.3 no-send files.

findings.claim: The no-send/public-action gate passed with failure_total 0 and no_send_byte_binding_failure_total 0.
findings.failure_mode: The certified no-send check binds the publish manifest and owner approval files, but it does not bind the public metadata surface that currently fails: .zenodo.json, manifest.json, checksums.txt, and RO-Crate hasPart parity. The gate can pass while a stale DOI manifest and missing Zenodo artifact remain public, which makes the no-send proof overclaim its coverage.
findings.required_repair: Extend the finite-model no-send runner/input so every public metadata artifact is existence-checked, hash-bound, v1.3.3-scoped, and DOI-free until owner approval; regenerate FINITE_MODEL_CHECKS_1_3_3.json only after those checks fail on stale DOI or missing public-surface artifacts.
